raw_case_text:
The patient was a male aged 56 years with comorbidities of diabetes and HIV. This individual was clinically and laboratory-compensated. The patient was using tenofovir, lamivudine, and efavirenz. His TCD4 lymphocyte count was measured at 1,163 cells, with a viral load that remained undetectable for a long period of time. However, hospitalization was required due to the onset of both dyspnea and asthenia. While a laboratory investigation via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) showed negative results for SARS-CoV-2 infection, a computed tomography (CT) examination of the chest showed a radiological pattern typically reported following the pulmonary involvement of SARS-CoV-2. Based on immunochromatographic analysis, the patient evolved as a reagent for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and immunoglobulin G (IgG) anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies. The patient was clinically compensated for respiratory infection, initially treated with ceftriaxone and clarithromycin for 3 days, and did not require other therapeutic measures to control the respiratory condition. Two days after hospital discharge (around 20 days after the beginning of respiratory symptoms) the patient developed complete hemiparesis with a predominance in the right arm and conduction aphasia. At that time, the patient scored 11 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale. An electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia, while a Doppler echocardiogram showed results within the normal range. Lumbar puncture was performed for cerebrospinal fluid (CS) analysis and was not compatible with a central nervous system infection or acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. 
Imaging examinations were also conducted, with CT of the skull showing a loss of differentiation between the white-gray substance, hypoattenuation of deep nuclei, and an extensive area of vascular territory in the left middle cerebral artery (Figure 1). 
A T1-weighted magnetic resonance sequence showed an area of hypointensity, with a high intrinsic cortical signal, and hyperintensity in the T2 sequence (Figure 2). A Doppler velocimetric study of the left carotid artery determined total/critical sub occlusion. These findings corroborated the clinical diagnosis of subacute ischemic stroke, with an estimated duration of 15 days.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 56-year-old male presenting with acute dyspnea and asthenia, followed 20 days later by right-sided hemiparesis and conduction aphasia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 56-year-old male was initially hospitalized for dyspnea and asthenia in the setting of acute respiratory infection treated with ceftriaxone and clarithromycin for three days. Two days after discharge (approximately 20 days from initial symptom onset), he acutely developed complete right-sided hemiparesis predominant in the right upper extremity and conduction aphasia, prompting emergent re-hospitalization.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diabetes mellitus; underlying chronic viral infection on long-term combination antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir, lamivudine, efavirenz); clinically and laboratory-compensated prior to index illness.
subjective.review_of_systems: Dyspnea, asthenia, acute right arm and leg weakness, and speech impairment (conduction aphasia); denies fever or seizure.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination: Complete right hemiparesis with predominance in the right arm, conduction aphasia; National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 11. Cardiovascular: Regular rhythm, sinus tachycardia.
objective.routine_investigations: Electrocardiogram: Sinus tachycardia. Doppler echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular function and structure. Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: Unremarkable, ruled out central nervous system infection or acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. Infectious serology: Positive for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies by immunochromatography; initial nasopharyngeal RT-PCR was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT: Ground-glass radiological pattern typical of SARS-CoV-2 pulmonary involvement. Cranial non-contrast CT: Loss of gray-white matter differentiation, hypoattenuation of deep nuclei, and an extensive ischemic territorial infarct in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA). Brain MRI: T1-weighted sequence showed hypointensity with high intrinsic cortical signal, and hyperintensity on T2-weighted sequence in the left MCA territory. Carotid Doppler ultrasonography: Critical sub-occlusion / total occlusion of the left internal carotid artery.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Subacute large-vessel ischemic stroke involving the left middle cerebral artery territory secondary to critical sub-occlusion/occlusion of the left internal carotid artery (NIHSS 11), occurring as a post-infectious thrombotic complication of SARS-CoV-2 infection (confirmed by positive IgM and IgG serology), in a patient with diabetes mellitus and well-controlled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; baseline CD4 count 1,163 cells/microL, undetectable viral load on tenofovir, lamivudine, efavirenz).
Course & Outcome: Respiratory infection stabilized following ceftriaxone and clarithromycin. Neurological deficits were managed supportively for subacute ischemic stroke with an estimated duration of 15 days.
